content: 1. The typical dosage range for ZOCOR (simvastatin) is between 5 mg and 40 mg per day. 2. In patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) or those at high risk for CHD, ZOCOR can be initiated alongside dietary modifications. 3. The recommended starting dose of ZOCOR is 10 mg or 20 mg once daily, administered in the evening. 4. For patients at high risk of CHD events due to existing CHD, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, history of stroke, or other cerebrovascular diseases, the recommended starting dose is 40 mg per day. 5. Lipid levels should be assessed after four weeks of therapy and periodically thereafter. 6. Due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis, particularly during the first year of treatment, the 80 mg dose of ZOCOR should be restricted to patients who have been taking simvastatin 80 mg chronically (e.g., for 12 months or more) without evidence of muscle toxicity. 7. Patients tolerating the 80 mg dose of ZOCOR who require initiation of an interacting drug contraindicated or associated with a dose cap for simvastatin should be switched to an alternative statin with a lower potential for drug-drug interactions. 8. Patients unable to achieve their LDL-C goal with the 40 mg dose of ZOCOR should not be titrated to the 80 mg dose but should instead be placed on alternative LDL-C-lowering treatments that provide greater efficacy. 9. For patients taking verapamil, diltiazem, or dronedarone, the dose of ZOCOR should not exceed 10 mg per day. 10. For patients taking amiodarone, amlodipine, or ranolazine, the dose of ZOCOR should not exceed 20 mg per day. 11. The recommended dosage of ZOCOR is 40 mg per day, administered in the evening. 12. ZOCOR should be used as an adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g., LDL apheresis) in specific patients or when such treatments are unavailable. 13. 14. ZOCOR dosage should not exceed 20 mg per day (or 40 mg per day for patients previously taking ZOCOR 80 mg/day chronically without muscle toxicity) when taken with lomitapide. 15. Since ZOCOR does not undergo significant renal excretion, dosage modification is generally unnecessary in patients with mild to moderate renal impairment. However, caution is advised in patients with severe renal impairment, who should start at 5 mg per day and be closely monitored. 16. Chinese patients taking simvastatin 40 mg co-administered with lipid-modifying doses (≥1 g/day) of niacin-containing products have an increased risk of myopathy. Caution should be exercised when treating Chinese patients with simvastatin doses exceeding 20 mg/day co-administered with niacin-containing products. 17. Chinese patients should not receive simvastatin 80 mg co-administered with lipid-modifying doses of niacin-containing products due to the dose-related risk of myopathy. 18. The cause of the increased risk of myopathy in Chinese patients is unknown, and it is unclear if this risk applies to other Asian populations. 19. Patients should be informed of the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis, and advised to promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness. 20. If symptoms of myopathy occur, treatment with ZOCOR should be discontinued immediately. 21. Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), an autoimmune myopathy, has been rarely associated with statin use. IMNM is characterized by persistent proximal muscle weakness, elevated serum creatine kinase, and muscle biopsy findings of necrotizing myopathy without significant inflammation, which improves with immunosuppressive agents. 22. All patients starting ZOCOR therapy or increasing their dose should be advised of the risk of myopathy and instructed to report any unexplained muscle symptoms, particularly if accompanied by malaise or fever. 23. ZOCOR therapy should be discontinued immediately if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. 24. In most cases, muscle symptoms and creatine kinase (CK) elevations resolve when treatment is promptly discontinued. 25. Periodic CK determinations may be considered in patients starting ZOCOR therapy or increasing their dose, but such monitoring does not guarantee prevention of myopathy. 26. Many patients who developed rhabdomyolysis while on simvastatin therapy had complicated medical histories, including renal insufficiency, often due to long-standing diabetes mellitus. These patients require closer monitoring. 27. ZOCOR therapy should be discontinued if markedly elevated CK levels occur or myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. 28. ZOCOR therapy should also be temporarily withheld in patients experiencing acute or serious conditions predisposing to renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis, such as sepsis, hypotension, major surgery, trauma, severe metabolic or electrolyte disorders, or uncontrolled epilepsy. 29. Simvastatin is metabolized by the cytochrome P450 isoform 3A4 (CYP3A4). Drugs that inhibit this pathway can increase plasma levels of simvastatin and the risk of myopathy. 30. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, voriconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, boceprevir, telaprevir, nefazodone, or grapefruit juice) with simvastatin is contraindicated. 31. If short-term treatment with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, simvastatin therapy must be suspended during the course of treatment. 32. Concomitant use of simvastatin with gemfibrozil, cyclosporine, or danazol is contraindicated due to an increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 33. Caution should be exercised when prescribing other fibrates with simvastatin, as these agents can cause myopathy when given alone, and the risk is increased when co-administered. 34. Cases of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis, have been reported with simvastatin co-administered with colchicine. Caution is advised when prescribing this combination. 35. Persistent increases in serum transaminases (to more than three times the upper limit of normal) have occurred in approximately 1% of patients receiving simvastatin in clinical studies. Therapy should be interrupted or discontinued if serious liver injury occurs. 36. Liver function tests should be performed before initiating treatment and thereafter when clinically indicated. 37. There have been rare postmarketing reports of fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure in patients taking statins, including simvastatin. Therapy should be promptly interrupted if serious liver injury occurs. 38. Moderate (less than three times the upper limit of normal) elevations in serum transaminases have been reported with simvastatin therapy. These changes are often transient and do not require treatment interruption. 39. Increases in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels have been reported with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, including ZOCOR. 40. In clinical trials, the most common adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation were gastrointestinal disorders, myalgia, and elevated liver enzymes. 41. The most commonly reported adverse reactions (≥5% incidence) in controlled clinical trials were upper respiratory infections, headache, abdominal pain, constipation, and nausea. 42. In a study involving adolescent patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, the most common adverse reactions were upper respiratory infections, headache, abdominal pain, and nausea. 43. Rare postmarketing reports of cognitive impairment (e.g., memory loss, forgetfulness, amnesia, confusion) have been associated with statin use. These issues are generally non-serious and reversible upon discontinuation. 44. Simvastatin therapy has not been associated with bleeding or changes in prothrombin time in patients not taking anticoagulants. However, in patients taking coumarin anticoagulants, prothrombin time should be monitored before starting simvastatin and during early therapy. 45. Concomitant administration of digoxin with simvastatin may result in a slight elevation in plasma digoxin concentrations. Patients taking digoxin should be monitored appropriately when simvastatin is initiated.
